questions.stem: Which of the following was a major initiative that helped India achieve self-sufficiency in food grains during the 1960s and 1970s?
questions.solution: The Green Revolution was a major initiative that helped India achieve self-sufficiency in food grains during the 1960s and 1970s. It involved the introduction of high-yielding variety seeds, chemical fertilizers, and improved irrigation techniques, which significantly increased agricultural production. The Golden Revolution focused on horticulture, Operation Flood was related to dairy development, and the Industrial Revolution was not a factor in food grain production during that time.

questions.stem: What is the name of the document that outlines how a nation's resources should be used?
questions.solution: The Five Year Plan is the document that outlines how a nation's resources should be used, as it provides a structured approach to resource allocation over a specific period. Perspective Plan and Industrial Policy Resolution focus more on long-term goals and sector-specific strategies, respectively, rather than detailing resource usage. Economic Reforms refer to changes in policies rather than a formal document outlining resource use.

questions.stem: Which policy in India aimed to reduce the concentration of land ownership?
questions.solution: Land ceiling was a policy designed to limit the amount of land any single individual could own, thus reducing the concentration of land in a few hands. The Green Revolution focused on increasing agricultural production through new technologies, not on land distribution. Operation Flood was aimed at boosting milk production and dairy development, while the Industrial Revolution was a broad historical period, not a specific policy in India.

questions.stem: Which of the following best explains why Nehru rejected the Soviet model of socialism?
choices: Because it did not allow democracy
questions.solution: Nehru rejected the Soviet model of socialism because it did not allow democracy, as it centralized power and restricted individual freedoms. The Soviet system was characterized by a single-party state and lack of political pluralism, which conflicted with Nehru's vision of a democratic society. The other options are incorrect because the Soviet model did not promote capitalism, did not entirely eliminate private property, and did emphasize industrialization as part of its development strategy.
